title: Harbor ferry pilot begins after weather delay

verified_facts.text: Bellwether City began a six-month electric ferry pilot on 12 August 2026.
The launch occurred nine days later than scheduled because high winds prevented required safety drills.
The vessel carries up to 80 passengers.
Officials estimate the pilot could reduce route emissions by 18 percent, but the result has not yet been measured.

sources_evidence.description: Harbor master weather and drill log

sources_evidence.provenance: Transit department model, not an observed result

required_disclosures.text: The 18 percent emissions figure is a projection, not a measured result.

quotes.speaker: Transit director Mira Sol
quotes.exact_text: The pilot will tell us what works on this route.

chronology.event: Original launch date; safety drills postponed due to high winds.

editorial_confidence.subject: pilot_launch
editorial_confidence.note: Confirmed by city and harbor records.

editorial_confidence.subject: emissions_reduction
editorial_confidence.note: Projection only; measurement will occur during the pilot.

other_editorial_judgment: Do not imply the weather delay was evidence of a safety defect.
